findings.failure_path: The version is bumped to 0.18.4 for release, but make test, the npm suite and the packaged-hook checks (H9, including whether skill-loading.py ships next to host-input.py) have not passed. If the package leaves out that helper, deduplication silently does nothing and the release goes out unverified.
findings.smallest_fix: Before tagging, finish make test, make npm-test, make npm-pack-verify, make npm-publish-dry and make npm-host-smoke, and record their output bound to this candidate. Also confirm the packed artifact contains hooks/skill-loading.py.

findings.failure_path: On the extraction-overflow path, a ValueError, TypeError or AttributeError (for example a non-dict payload) prints 'Delivery handoff reminder unavailable', which is the wrong hook's message.
findings.smallest_fix: Choose the fallback message based on sys.argv[1] so the extraction lane shows the extraction 'check incomplete' notice.

concern_results.conclusion: The strict whole-session audit still refuses partial evidence. On overflow, only a complete current context is used, and only positive evidence counts (delivery_eligible, extraction requested_skills). Absence re-raises TranscriptTruncated or produces a notice. Extraction uses requested_skills, which matches the existing whole-session behaviour.

Markers reuse State's owned-directory, no-follow and atomic mkdir claim. A symlinked state root raises ValueError and falls back to the notice; the test checks that the symlink target stays empty. Markers only control whether the notice is shown. They cannot skip checks or grant permission.

If the optional helper import fails, identity is missing or state is unsafe, the notice is still shown. The shell falls back to the original notice if the helper fails. One small copy problem: a non-object payload on the extraction-overflow path shows the delivery-handoff 'unavailable' message instead of the extraction message. The shell has already parsed the input as an object, so this is unlikely in practice.

Subprocess tests cover repeated notices, concurrency, actor, session and transcript replacement, unsafe state, positive recovery on both hosts, unknown current context, and the size check before parsing. The pending/failed current-context cases only use product-rd-workflow; there is no pending extraction Skill request case. The full make test run and the npm lanes are recorded as not yet passing.
The transcript command output is unchanged. The new 'extraction-overflow' subcommand is additive. The import of skill-loading.py is optional and caught.
Version 0.18.4 is untagged and unpublished. Checks for the packaged hooks (H9) and the release (H10) are still pending, and there is no evidence yet that the built package includes skill-loading.py.
Notices contain no transcript text, identities or paths. A notice is suppressed only after a successful claim. If state is unavailable, the notice appears on every Stop.
The self-review openly lists the unfinished verification. The plan's H9 and H10 rows stay pending. Readiness for publication is not yet supported by evidence.
Caller-supplied session, actor and path values only affect whether the notice is deduplicated. The stop_hook_active guard on handoff blocks is preserved and tested.

The work is on a feature branch with a plan, a RED baseline and a source-register entry. The root contract requires make test and the package validation to pass before completion. The evidence says those have not passed yet; this is reported as a finding.
